title: The module $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ of a finite locally free morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a locally free $\mathcal{O}_S$-module of rank $d$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and for every $s\in S$ with residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] the canonical map $(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)_s\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S,s}}\kappa(s)\to \Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s})$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply the existing source-library theorem Scheme.Modules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pushforward_unit f d, already attached to this node in lean_audit, to prove the rank assertion. It includes the finite-projective affine argument and the identification of rank with fibre degree, using the degree hypothesis [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

Choose an affine neighbourhood V of s. Apply the existing source-library theorem Scheme.Hom.exists_ringEquiv_stalk_pushforward_tensorProduct_fiber, already attached to this node in lean_audit, to obtain the canonical ring isomorphism and its formula for sections on V. Its affine-morphism hypothesis follows from finiteness in [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

For all neighbourhoods U of s, restriction to the fibre is compatible with restriction of sections, by Scheme.Hom.map_appLE. These maps define a cocone on the neighbourhood diagram, hence a ring map q from the pushforward stalk. The germ followed by q is the restriction to the fibre, by colimit.ι_desc. The source theorem Scheme.Hom.isLocalization_stalk_pushforward identifies this stalk as a localization of the sections on V. By IsLocalization.ringHom_ext, the composite of the left tensor inclusion with the isomorphism of Step 2 equals q: both agree on sections on V by the formula of Step 2 with scalar one. That formula applied to the section one also gives the value on 1 tensor k. Multiplicativity now proves the displayed formula for every U, every section a and every scalar k.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism
finite locally free of degree
$d$. Then $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a locally free $\mathcal{O}_S$-module of rank $d$,
and for every $s\in S$ the canonical map
$(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)_s\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S,s}}\kappa(s)\to \Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s})$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Both assertions are local on $S$, so let $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq S$
be an affine open. The morphism $f$ is finite, hence affine, so
$f^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ with $B=\Gamma(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal{O}_X)$, and
$f_*\mathcal{O}_X|_V$ is the quasi-coherent module $\widetilde B$ attached to the
$A$-module $B$. Since $f$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation
([def-pc-finite-locally-free]), $B$ is a finite $A$-module, flat over $A$, and
a finitely presented $A$-algebra; a finite algebra of finite presentation is a
finitely presented module, and a finitely presented flat module is finite
projective. Hence $f_*\mathcal{O}_X|_V=\widetilde B$ is finite locally free.

*The fibres.* Let $s\in V$ correspond to the prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$.
Fibre products of affine schemes are spectra of tensor products
([def-pc-base-change]), so
$X_s=f^{-1}(V)\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(s))$
and $\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s})=B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$, the map
$B\to\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s})$ being restriction of functions. The stalk of
$\widetilde B$ at $s$ is the localization $B_{\mathfrak p}=B\otimes_AA_{\mathfrak p}$,
so

$$
(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)_s\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S,s}}\kappa(s)
=B_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(s)=B\otimes_A\kappa(s)
=\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s}),
$$

and this composite is the canonical map of the statement, which is therefore
an isomorphism.

*The rank.* The rank of the finite projective module $B$ at $s$ is
$\dim_{\kappa(s)}B\otimes_A\kappa(s)=\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s})=d$
by the definition of degree $d$ ([def-pc-finite-locally-free]). Hence
$f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is locally free of rank $d$.
